chunks: And by this chain, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Isma'il ibn Jabir — he said:
I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the water that nothing can render ritually impure. He said: 'A kurr.' I said: 'And what is the kurr?' He said: 'Three spans by three spans.'

key_terms.أَشْبَارٍ: spans (sing. shibr) — a hand-span, the distance from the outstretched tip of the thumb to the tip of the little finger
key_terms.الْمَاءِ: water — the subject of this tahara ruling
key_terms.كُرٌّ: kurr — a unit of volumetric measure; the minimum quantity of water immune to ritual impurity
key_terms.يُنَجِّسُهُ: renders it ritually impure — from Form II verb najjasa, to cause najasah

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum volume of water (kurr) that cannot be made ritually impure, according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: Isma'il ibn Jabir narrates that he asked Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about the minimum volume of water that cannot be rendered ritually impure by contact with filth. The Imam identified this as a kurr and defined it as three spans (shibr) by three spans — establishing the foundational volumetric criterion in Shia jurisprudence for water that resists ritual contamination.
